title: Per-request Telemetry Synchronizer for Inference Nodes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Per-request inference metrics are arriving in two distinct pipelines (Prometheus scrape frames and OTel metrics spans) with inconsistent labels and sampling. This leads to noisy SLO calculation, misattributed latency, and gaps in per-tenant billing.

Goal: Build a lightweight Per-request Telemetry Synchronizer (sidecar) that runs colocated with inference worker processes to:
- Attach deterministic request identifiers and trace hooks to both Prometheus-style counters/histograms and OTel metric spans.
- Buffer and backpressure metrics during short pressure spikes to avoid cardinality-induced throttling downstream.
- Normalize labels (model_id, route, variant, tenant_id, shard) into a canonical KPI envelope and emit an OTLP-compatible metric stream + Prometheus scrape target.
- Offer configurable sampling rules and sticky deterministic sampling for sporadic high-cardinality attributes (e.g., prompt_hash).

Non-goals: This ticket does not change storage schemas or downstream rollups; it focuses on producing better, consistent telemetry at the source.

Design notes:
- Sidecar exposes a /metrics endpoint for Prometheus and an OTLP exporter to the telemetry gateway.
- Uses a small in-memory ring buffer with per-tenant backpressure counters; when buffer reaches thresholds, metrics are aggregated (histogram bucketing) and lower-priority labels are dropped.
- Deterministic sample hashing is seeded by tenant_id + route + model_version to preserve reproducible sampling across restarts.
- Trace hooks: when inference runtime emits a request start/end, sidecar attaches the active trace/span and enriches the metric envelope with trace_id and span_id for causal linking.
- Label canonicalization mapping allows renaming (e.g., path -> route) and annotation of deprecated labels for migration.

Why a sidecar: colocated sidecar minimizes telemetry loss at the worker boundary, preserves per-request context (KV cache state, model pins), and enables immediate enrichment without touching the runtime core.

Performance constraints: sidecar must add <1% p99 latency overhead for typical request sizes and maintain <200MB memory for 100k rps worker with default sampling enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar binary with Prometheus /metrics endpoint and OTLP exporter producing canonical KPI envelope
Per-request trace_id/span_id present in at least 95% of enriched metric envelopes for sampled requests
Deterministic sampling respects seed and maintains stable sample set across restarts (integration test)
Backpressure logic triggers aggregation and label-dropping without data loss when buffer threshold exceeded (fault injection test)
End-to-end test demonstrating improved latency attribution in dashboard: per-route p50/p95/p99 aligns with traces for a synthetic workload
Memory and CPU usage under 1% overhead for representative staging load (performance benchmark)
Docs: runbook, config reference, migration guide for label canonicalization published to Confluence
tasks: Design: finalize metric envelope schema and label canonicalization mapping
Implementation: sidecar skeleton, /metrics endpoint, OTLP exporter
Instrumentation: add trace hook and request lifecycle API in runtime to call sidecar
Buffering: implement ring buffer + backpressure + label-dropping policy
Sampling: deterministic sampling component with seed persist/restore
E2E tests: synthetic workload to validate attribution and SLO alignment
Perf tests: run with 100k rps synthetic harness in staging nodes
Docs: Confluence PR and runbook; example Helm config for Dedicated and Private deployments
Rollout: canary deploy to staging -> dedicated sandbox -> gradual production rollout
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased cardinality if sidecar emits more detailed labels. Mitigation: default label blacklist + deterministic sampling and aggregation under backpressure.

Risk: Sidecar crash could drop metrics. Mitigation: implement soft-fail mode where runtime falls back to legacy emitter and sidecar crash is surfaced to Sentry and metrics (internal_telemetry.sidecar_down).
Risk: Latency impact on fast-path. Mitigation: non-blocking emission using bounded queue and async worker threads; measure overhead via p99 microbenchmarks.
Risk: Compatibility with existing telemetry gateway schema. Mitigation: provide schema translation layer and compatibility mode flag; coordinate with telemetry-gateway owners (ENG-42111).
